title: Mombasa vs Dar es Salaam vs Lobito: The Race for Inland Africa's Cargo | The Six, Ep. 9
lede: Mombasa moved a record 45.45 million tonnes in 2025, including 15.88 million tonnes of transit cargo for inland countries. Dar es Salaam's transit cargo rose 17% to 14.61 million tonnes, and on the Atlantic, backers have committed $1.3 billion to a rail line from Zambia's Copperbelt to Lobito. This episode follows the three corridors competing for East and Central Africa's trade.
keyPoints: Mombasa handled a record 45.45 million tonnes in 2025, up 10.9%, with transit cargo up 19.5% to 15.88 million tonnes (Kenya Ports Authority). Uganda accounts for more than 65% of that transit, about 10.91 million tonnes.

Kenya broke ground on the 475 km Naivasha–Malaba standard gauge extension in March 2026 and began construction in July; Uganda's 273 km Malaba–Kampala line, priced at €2.7 billion, is due in 2028 (The Star).

Dar es Salaam handled 33.71 million tonnes in FY2025/26, up 21.5%; transit rose 17% to 14.61 million tonnes, with DR Congo at 7.77 million tonnes, Zambia 3.41 million and Rwanda 2.18 million (Daily News, Tanzania).
Kenya's State Department for EAC estimates the country loses 5–8% of high-value transit cargo a year, mainly to Dar es Salaam (The Star, June 2026).

Lobito Atlantic Railway closed $753 million of loans in December 2025 (U.S. DFC $553m, DBSA $200m) to lift capacity to 4.6 million tonnes a year; the new Zambia line, costed at up to $5 billion, has $1.3 billion committed and targets completion in 2030.
